fruits.extendedStory: Roughly 49 metres of height, and a building that reached its present form during 1572. Gothic work, and you read that off its windows rather than its plan. Glass occupies so much wall that masonry seems reduced to framing. Choose a bright morning and step inside. Illumination performs whatever ornament achieves elsewhere.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Abtei misst etwa 49 Meter, der heutige Bau stammt von 1572. Sie ist gotisch, und der Stil zeigt sich in den Fenstern. So viel Glas steckt in diesen Wänden, dass der Stein wie ein Rahmen dafür wirkt. Geh an einem hellen Tag hinein. Das Licht leistet hier, was anderswo der Schmuck leistet.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Roughly 49 metres of height, and a building that reached its present form during 1572. Gothic work, and you read that off its windows rather than its plan. Glass occupies so much wall that masonry seems reduced to framing. Choose a bright morning and step inside. Illumination performs whatever ornament achieves elsewhere.

localizedStory.de: Eine gotische Kirche von etwa 49 Metern, deren heutiger Bau von 1572 stammt.
localizedStory.en: A Gothic church rising about 49 metres, whose present building dates from 1572.

fruits.name: Bath Abbey
fruits.story: A Gothic church rising about 49 metres, whose present building dates from 1572.

fruits.extendedStory: Water rises here from below without anyone pumping it, and it is warm when it arrives. The Romans built around that fact, and their stonework is what you go down to see. The buildings you meet at street level came much later, finished in 1897, and John Wood had a hand in the surroundings. Two eras stand on top of each other here, and the water is older than either.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Hier steigt Wasser von unten auf, ohne dass jemand pumpt, und es ist warm, wenn es ankommt. Die Römer bauten um diese Tatsache herum, und ihr Steinwerk ist das, wofür man hinuntergeht. Was man auf Straßenhöhe sieht, kam viel später, 1897 fertig, und John Wood hatte an der Umgebung Anteil. Zwei Zeiten stehen hier übereinander, und das Wasser ist älter als beide.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Water rises here from below without anyone pumping it, and it is warm when it arrives. The Romans built around that fact, and their stonework is what you go down to see. The buildings you meet at street level came much later, finished in 1897, and John Wood had a hand in the surroundings. Two eras stand on top of each other here, and the water is older than either.

localizedStory.de: Heißes Wasser steigt hier noch immer von selbst auf, so wie schon für die Römer.
localizedStory.en: Hot water still comes up here on its own, as it did for the Romans.

fruits.name: The Roman Baths
fruits.story: Hot water still comes up here on its own, as it did for the Romans.

fruits.extendedStory: John Wood the Younger finished these in 1769, and a grand ball in 1771 got them going. Five Whitefriars crystal chandeliers hang above dancing space for 500. Overnight on 25 to 26 April 1942, Baedeker raids gutted everything within. Whatever hangs up there today had to be replaced. Outer walls endured; the interior is restoration work throughout.

localizedExtendedStory.de: John Wood der Jüngere baute diese Säle 1769, und 1771 eröffneten sie mit einem großen Ball. Der Ballsaal fasst 500 Menschen, unter fünf Kristallleuchtern aus Whitefriars. In der Nacht vom 25. auf den 26. April 1942 brannten die Baedeker-Angriffe das Innere aus. Was heute dort hängt, musste ersetzt werden. Die Hülle blieb, alles darin ist Wiederherstellung.
localizedExtendedStory.en: John Wood the Younger finished these in 1769, and a grand ball in 1771 got them going. Five Whitefriars crystal chandeliers hang above dancing space for 500. Overnight on 25 to 26 April 1942, Baedeker raids gutted everything within. Whatever hangs up there today had to be replaced. Outer walls endured; the interior is restoration work throughout.

localizedStory.de: Fünf Kristallleuchter hängen über einem Ballsaal, der 500 Menschen fasst.
localizedStory.en: Five crystal chandeliers hang over a ballroom that holds 500 people.

fruits.name: The Assembly Rooms
fruits.story: Five crystal chandeliers hang over a ballroom that holds 500 people.

fruits.extendedStory: Robert Adam drew it, and 1774 saw it standing. Neoclassical proportions, borrowed from Rome, govern how it looks. Shopfronts occupy both parapets, which is unusual. Cross over and no water appears anywhere, just windows and doorways either hand. Descend to the bank afterwards and you finally grasp that you were walking above a river.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Robert Adam entwarf sie, 1774 stand sie. Er arbeitete klassizistisch, ein Stil, der seine Maße aus Rom holt. Ungewöhnlich ist die Ladenzeile auf beiden Brüstungen. Geht man hinüber, sieht man kein Wasser, nur Schaufenster. Erst unten am Ufer begreift man, dass man auf einer Brücke war.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Robert Adam drew it, and 1774 saw it standing. Neoclassical proportions, borrowed from Rome, govern how it looks. Shopfronts occupy both parapets, which is unusual. Cross over and no water appears anywhere, just windows and doorways either hand. Descend to the bank afterwards and you finally grasp that you were walking above a river.

localizedStory.de: Auf beiden Seiten dieser Brücke stehen Läden, sodass man den Fluss beim Überqueren gar nicht sieht.
localizedStory.en: Shops line both sides of this bridge, so crossing it you cannot see the river at all.

fruits.name: Pulteney Bridge
fruits.story: Shops line both sides of this bridge, so crossing it you cannot see the river at all.

fruits.extendedStory: Thomas Baldwin began this room and lost the job in 1793 when his money ran out. John Palmer finished it, and it opened on 28 December 1795. Water is pumped up from the hot springs and comes out of a marble vase, and people drink it. Jane Austen knew the room and used it in Northanger Abbey and Persuasion. Every creature in Bath was to be seen here at one hour or another.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Thomas Baldwin begann diesen Saal und verlor 1793 den Auftrag, als sein Geld ausging. John Palmer vollendete ihn, und am 28. Dezember 1795 wurde eröffnet. Wasser wird aus den heißen Quellen heraufgepumpt, tritt aus einer Marmorvase aus, und man trinkt es. Jane Austen kannte den Saal und verwendete ihn in Northanger Abbey und Persuasion. Alles, was in Bath Beine hatte, war hier irgendwann zu sehen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Thomas Baldwin began this room and lost the job in 1793 when his money ran out. John Palmer finished it, and it opened on 28 December 1795. Water is pumped up from the hot springs and comes out of a marble vase, and people drink it. Jane Austen knew the room and used it in Northanger Abbey and Persuasion. Every creature in Bath was to be seen here at one hour or another.

localizedStory.de: Aus einer Marmorvase fließt hier Heilwasser, direkt aus den heißen Quellen darunter heraufgepumpt.
localizedStory.en: A marble vase pours out spa water here, pumped straight up from the hot springs below.

fruits.name: The Pump Room
fruits.story: A marble vase pours out spa water here, pumped straight up from the hot springs below.

fruits.extendedStory: Early eighteenth-century laying out, Georgian throughout, and John Wood the Elder ran it. Number 9 on the south side he kept back for himself, sighted along his obelisk toward that long front opposite. Beau Nash raised the obelisk during 1738, honouring Frederick, Prince of Wales. Seventy feet it measured, until an 1815 gale removed its top. Queen Caroline, wife of George II, supplies the name.

localizedExtendedStory.de: John Wood der Ältere legte dies im frühen achtzehnten Jahrhundert an, im georgianischen Stil. Nummer 9 behielt er für sich, an der Südseite, auf einer Linie mit seinem Obelisken und der langen Front gegenüber. Beau Nash stellte diesen Obelisken 1738 für Friedrich, Prinz von Wales, auf. Er maß 70 Fuß, bis 1815 ein Sturm die Spitze nahm. Der Platz trägt den Namen von Königin Caroline, der Frau Georgs II.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Early eighteenth-century laying out, Georgian throughout, and John Wood the Elder ran it. Number 9 on the south side he kept back for himself, sighted along his obelisk toward that long front opposite. Beau Nash raised the obelisk during 1738, honouring Frederick, Prince of Wales. Seventy feet it measured, until an 1815 gale removed its top. Queen Caroline, wife of George II, supplies the name.

localizedStory.de: Hier steht ein Obelisk, dem 1815 ein Sturm die Spitze nahm und der nie wieder erhöht wurde.
localizedStory.en: An obelisk stands here that lost its top to a gale in 1815, and was never made tall again.

fruits.name: Queen Square
fruits.story: An obelisk stands here that lost its top to a gale in 1815, and was never made tall again.

fruits.extendedStory: Charles Hansom built this in 1863, in the manner called Gothic Revival. That means Victorians looking back at medieval building and doing it again on purpose. The pointed arches and the spire are quotations, not inheritance. It belongs to John the Evangelist. In a city known for its Georgian streets, this is the century afterwards arguing for a different past.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Charles Hansom baute dies 1863, in der Weise, die man Neugotik nennt. Das heißt: Viktorianer schauten auf das Mittelalter zurück und machten es absichtlich noch einmal. Spitzbögen und Turmhelm sind Zitate, kein Erbe. Sie gehört Johannes dem Evangelisten. In einer Stadt der georgianischen Straßenzüge argumentiert hier das folgende Jahrhundert für eine andere Vergangenheit.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Charles Hansom built this in 1863, in the manner called Gothic Revival. That means Victorians looking back at medieval building and doing it again on purpose. The pointed arches and the spire are quotations, not inheritance. It belongs to John the Evangelist. In a city known for its Georgian streets, this is the century afterwards arguing for a different past.

localizedStory.de: Eine Kirche von 1863 von Charles Hansom, gebaut, um vier Jahrhunderte älter zu wirken.
localizedStory.en: A church of 1863 by Charles Hansom, built to look four centuries older than it is.

fruits.name: Saint John the Evangelist RC
fruits.story: A church of 1863 by Charles Hansom, built to look four centuries older than it is.

fruits.extendedStory: Trains ran under this roof from 1870 until the station closed in 1966. It is one great span of iron and glass, and it now shelters a market. Growers began selling here in September 1997, monthly at the start. Demand pushed it to twice a month from October 1998, and to every week from May 2002. A building that stopped having a use found another one.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Von 1870 bis zur Schließung 1966 fuhren unter diesem Dach Züge. Es ist eine weite Spannweite aus Eisen und Glas und überdacht heute einen Markt. Erzeuger verkaufen hier seit September 1997, anfangs monatlich. Die Nachfrage machte ab Oktober 1998 zwei Termine im Monat daraus und ab Mai 2002 jede Woche. Ein Bau ohne Zweck fand einen neuen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Trains ran under this roof from 1870 until the station closed in 1966. It is one great span of iron and glass, and it now shelters a market. Growers began selling here in September 1997, monthly at the start. Demand pushed it to twice a month from October 1998, and to every week from May 2002. A building that stopped having a use found another one.

localizedStory.de: Erzeuger verkaufen unter dem Eisen- und Glasdach eines Bahnhofs, der 1966 schloss.
localizedStory.en: Growers sell under the iron and glass roof of a railway station that shut in 1966.
